text.aria-label: Title text 'A power model trained on ERA5 makes smaller errors than the same model trained on ENS weather, up to day 6 ahead (one held-out year, nine generators)'

g.text: A power model trained on ERA5 makes smaller errors than the same model trained on ENS weather, up to day 6 ahead (one held-out year, nine generators)

text.aria-label: Subtitle text 'Mean absolute error of the forecast built from the average of the ENS members' weather, points of the generator's capacity (smaller is better), by how many days ahead the forecast is. ERA5: ECMWF's estimate of past weather. ENS: ECMWF's 51-member ensemble weather forecast. Every model on these charts is an XGBoost model given the same weather columns and no calendar or power-history columns. 6 solar farms and 3 wind farms; 53 ENS runs, one every 7 days, July 2025 to June 2026. Intervals come from re-drawing whole months at random and fitting with different random seeds. Dot: estimate. Line: 95% interval. Grey tick: the ERA5-trained model given ERA5 weather at the valid time instead of a forecast (not a forecast; it shows how much of the error comes from forecast weather). Grey dot: climatology.'
text.tspan: Mean absolute error of the forecast built from the average of the ENS members' weather, points of the generator's capacity (smaller is better), by how many days ahead the forecast is.

ERA5: ECMWF's estimate of past weather. ENS: ECMWF's 51-member ensemble weather forecast. Every model on these charts is an XGBoost model given the same weather columns and no calendar or power-history columns.
6 solar farms and 3 wind farms; 53 ENS runs, one every 7 days, July 2025 to June 2026. Intervals come from re-drawing whole months at random and fitting with different random seeds.

Dot: estimate. Line: 95% interval. Grey tick: the ERA5-trained model given ERA5 weather at the valid time instead of a forecast (not a forecast; it shows how much of the error comes from forecast weather). Grey dot: climatology.
